previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: An elderly woman with a history of chronic diastolic heart failure, transfusion-dependent anemia likely due to myelodysplastic syndrome, and recurrent venous thromboembolism on warfarin was admitted with acute-on-chronic left chest and shoulder pain and hypoxia. She was found to have volume overload contributing to acute on chronic diastolic heart failure, evidenced by pleural effusions, crackles on exam, and elevated liver enzymes, managed with IV furosemide and transition to home torsemide. A catheter-associated urinary tract infection with Citrobacter amalonaticus and Enterococcus was treated with IV ceftriaxone, then oral cefpodoxime and amoxicillin based on sensitivities. Her INR was subtherapeutic at 1.2, so she was bridged with enoxaparin and warfarin, achieving a therapeutic INR of 2.4 at discharge. She received one unit of packed red blood cells for symptomatic anemia. A brief episode of symptomatic bradycardia was attributed to a vasovagal event and resolved spontaneously. She was discharged home with home health services on a 7-day antibiotic course, continued anticoagulation, and instructions to monitor weight and follow up with her providers.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ with PMH of transfusion dependent anemia 
___ presumed myelodysplastic syndrome, chronic abd pain, dCHF, 
recurrent DVT/PE on warfarin, chronic left chest and left 
shoulder pain due to myofascial pain vs. atypical arthritis who 
presents with shoulder pain and pulm edema c/f CHF exacerbation.

#Acute-on-Chronic Shoulder Pain: ___ radiographs 
suggesting shows severe glenohumeral joint and moderately severe 
AC joint osteoarthritis. Lack of inflammation on exam makes 
crystal disease or septic joint unlikely. Pt has received 
cortisone injections as outpt in past, and has had an extensive 
workup for the same shoulder pain. Trops neg x 2 on admission, 
making cardiac etiology less likely. Pt was treated with Tylenol 
___ q6, Oxycodone 5mg q6 PRN, and a Lidocaine patch. Her pain 
improved over the course of her admission. 

#Acute on Chronic CHF Exacerbation: CXR on admission had 
evidence of pulm edema. BNP 156. Trops neg x 2. EKG with no 
changes. Pt had a foley placed in the ED for urine output 
monitoring, and was serially diuresed with 40mg IV lasix. The 
foley was removed on hospital day 2. She initially required 2L 
NC O2 to maintain her oxygen saturation. As diuresis progressed, 
she was weaned from supplemental O2. Discharge weight 71.4kg. 

#Hypokalemia: K 2.9 on admission, received 20 IV K in the ED 
with increase to 3.3. K was repleted orally as needed on a daily 
basis. Discharge K 4.0.

#Diarrhea: On day of discharge, pt reported having 2 episodes of 
loose stools. A sample was collected for C. diff testing, which 
was pending at time of discharge. 

#Anemia: Transfusion dependent, likely ___ MDS per outpatient 
records. She reportedly gets 2 units of RBCs at 4 week intervals 
per hematology. Most recent outpatient 2u pRBC were ___. 
Hgb 9.4 on admission. Pt did not require transfusion on this 
admission.

#Asymptomatic pyuria: UA was significant for positive nitrites, 
13 WBC and few bacteria on admission. Urine culture grew >100k 
gram negative rods (speciation pending on discharged). Pt 
received CTX in ED, but on further questioning was not 
complaining of any urinary symptoms. Thus, antibiotics were not 
continued, and the foley cathether that was inserted in the ED 
was removed on hospital day 2. 

#H/o DVT/PE: Continued home warfarin 2mg, remained therapeutic 
for goal INR 1.5-2.5 (per ___ clinic records).

# H/o Gastritis/esophagitis: Continued home omeprazole 

# H/O GLAUCOMA: Continued home timolol, latanoprost.

===================
TRANSITIONAL ISSUES
===================
- On day of discharge, pt reported having 2 episodes of loose 
stools. A sample was collected for C. diff testing, which was 
pending at time of discharge. (Addendum - this was normal).
- Pt has had previous cortisone shots as an outpatient, and 
would potentially benefit from another injection
- Code status: a discussion was had with the patient's son (and 
HCP) during which he expressed that it would be ok to provide 
cardiac resuscitation for his mother, but did not want her to be 
intubated. Followup on this code status discussion would be 
helpful, as a status of only DNI is not typical and intubation 
often follows cardiac resuscitation

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  Chest radiograph

INDICATION:  ___ woman presenting with lower extremity swelling and
chest pain.  Evaluate for pulmonary edema.

TECHNIQUE:  Upright Chest PA and lateral

COMPARISON:  Portable chest radiograph dated ___.  PA and
lateral chest radiograph dated ___.

FINDINGS: 

Bilateral, left worse than right lower lobe opacities with blurring of the
diaphragm silhouettes could be a combination of edema and/or
infection/aspiration.  Prominence of the interstitium may correspond to a
component of chronic interstitial changes noted on the prior head CT as well
as edema and/or infection.  The heart remains enlarged.  The descending
thoracic aorta is slightly tortuous.  No evidence of a pneumothorax.  The
thoracic spine is severely curved to the right, likely reflecting a degree is
scoliosis and positional changes.  This results in slight distortion of the
chest cage and altered appearance of the changes in the hemithorax.  No large
pleural effusion but there may be a small left pleural effusion.  Degenerative
changes in both glenohumeral joints as well as the left acromioclavicular
joint are severe.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Findings consistent with volume overload and/or heart failure.
2.  Sequelae of chronic aspiration and/or concurrent infection is possible in
the appropriate clinical situation.

EXAMINATION:  UNILAT LOWER EXT VEINS LEFT

INDICATION:  ___ woman with a history of prior DVT, now presenting
with left leg pain/swelling that is worse than the right.  Evaluate for deep
venous thrombosis.

on the left lower extremity veins.

There is normal compressibility, flow, and augmentation of the left common

the posterior tibial and peroneal veins.

There is normal respiratory variation in the common femoral veins bilaterally.
